answer: Proof-of-space registration resists sybils: each identity must dedicate a unique block of storage and periodically prove it still holds that data, so the binding cost is disk capacity, not clock speed. A farm minting a thousand fakes must provision a thousand distinct juniper-filled plots at once — capacity cannot be shared, since each proof is keyed to the identity. An honest agent fences one meadow of space and proves it cheaply; the attacker's cost grows linearly with identity count, and idle fakes keep burning capacity at the jetty until the swarm is uneconomic.
